question: What three disciplines form the foundation of nursing informatics?
explanation: Nursing informatics merges clinical nursing concepts with data and computer systems to optimize information handling. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h1)

question: The primary goal of nursing informatics is to manage what element in practice?
explanation: Informatics focuses on processing raw healthcare data all the way up to actionable knowledge and wisdom for better care. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h1)

question: How do electronic health records help prevent medication errors?

options.A: By replacing the need for qualified nurses
options.B: By eliminating the need for doctors' prescriptions
options.C: By providing automated allergy and dose alerts
options.D: By automatically purchasing drugs from pharmacies

explanation: Software alerts warn clinicians immediately if a prescribed medication conflicts with a patient allergy or safe dosage limits. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h2)

question: A nurse uses a barcode scanner before giving a drug to ensure what safety measure?

options.A: The right patient receives the right medication
options.B: The drug manufacturer gets immediate sales data
options.C: The hospital pharmacy bills the patient correctly
options.D: The doctor is notified that treatment is finished

explanation: Scanning patient wristbands and medication packages acts as a final safety barrier against administration mistakes. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is a major disadvantage of traditional paper-based nursing documentation?

options.A: It automatically deletes records after one week
options.C: It is prone to loss and poor legibility
options.D: It stops doctors from writing prescriptions

explanation: Paper records can be physically misplaced, destroyed, or hard to read due to handwriting variations. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h3)

question: How do electronic documentation systems improve clinical workflow efficiency?

options.A: By letting nurses skip physical patient assessments
options.B: By allowing simultaneous chart access for multiple users
options.C: By removing the need for verbal shift handovers
options.D: By printing all patient notes automatically every hour

explanation: Digital charts do not live in one physical folder, so various team members can review or update details at the same time. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the main benefit of centralized electronic care plans?

options.A: Updates are instantly visible to all authorized personnel
options.B: Patients can edit their own medical diagnosis codes
options.C: Hospital management can monitor staff break times
options.D: External insurance companies can block treatments

explanation: Centralized systems keep the entire multidisciplinary team aligned with real-time updates on patient status. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is fast lab result notification through informatics important for patient care?

options.A: It allows nurses to perform laboratory blood tests
options.B: It speeds up medical decision-making and interventions
options.C: It prevents patients from asking questions about tests
options.D: It reduces the total salary cost for laboratory staff

explanation: Quick access to test results lets the healthcare team start necessary treatments without waiting for physical document delivery. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h4)

question: Where are clinical decision support tools typically embedded in modern hospitals?

options.A: On the front gate notice board of the facility
options.B: Inside the personal notebooks of head nurses
options.C: Within the electronic health record system
options.D: On physical posters placed in hospital canteens

explanation: Embedding guidelines inside electronic records ensures nurses can access evidence right when planning or delivering care. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h5)

question: How does informatics help close the gap between research and bedside practice?

options.A: By replacing clinical judgment with strict robot actions
options.B: By providing instant prompts and clinical guidelines
options.C: By banning traditional nursing practices completely
options.D: By forcing patients to read medical journals daily

explanation: Software prompts remind nurses of current evidence-based protocols during routine assessments and care planning. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which feature in informatics systems tracks who views or edits a patient file?
explanation: Audit trails record user activity logs, showing exactly who accessed or modified patient information and when. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why are strict access controls necessary in electronic health record systems?

options.A: To protect patient privacy and maintain data security
options.B: To prevent patients from paying their hospital bills
options.C: To slow down the internet connection in wards
options.D: To stop junior nurses from reading doctor notes

explanation: Access controls ensure that only authorized healthcare personnel can view sensitive personal and clinical information. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is a major emerging technology in modern digital health care?
explanation: AI and telehealth represent the cutting edge of modern healthcare delivery, expanding access and analytical power. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why should bedside nurses be involved in designing new healthcare technologies?

options.A: So they can work as computer programming experts
options.B: To ensure the tools match real clinical needs
options.C: So they can sell software to other hospitals
options.D: To take over the jobs of hospital IT engineers

explanation: Nurses understand daily workflow realities best, making their input vital for creating practical and safe healthcare tools. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h7)
